key_insight: Sparse, user-edited keyframes can serve as a simple, expressive control signal for video super-resolution: correcting a few frames and intelligently propagating those edits yields high-quality, consistent videos while enabling interactive correction.
problem_solved: Traditional VSR models act like black boxes at inference time—users cannot reliably correct unexpected artifacts or guide restoration. SparkVSR addresses the need for controllable, interactive VSR that preserves temporal consistency while minimizing user effort.
method: Treat a small set of high-quality keyframes (optionally edited by the user) as explicit control inputs for the entire video.
Learn a sparse keyframe propagation module that transfers detail and corrections from keyframes to neighboring frames while enforcing temporal consistency.
Design for interactive use: low-latency propagation and refinement so users can iteratively edit a few frames and immediately see global improvements.
impact: Enables human-in-the-loop VSR workflows where practitioners can fix artifacts with minimal edits, improving trust, editability, and practical deployment of VSR in production and creative tools.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: user edits a few sparse keyframes → propagation module → full super-resolved video (highlight flow of information).
Before/after frame comparisons showing artifact correction with and without keyframe edits.
Heatmap or arrow visualization of propagation strength/flow from keyframes across time (sparsity vs. influence).
Tradeoff chart: number of keyframes vs. quality improvement and latency (showing diminishing returns).
paper_title: SparkVSR: Interactive Video Super-Resolution via Sparse Keyframe Propagation
paper_authors: Jiongze Yu, Xiangbo Gao, Pooja Verlani, Akshay Gadde, Yilin Wang
